name: STM32L151C8T6
title: Ultra-low-power Arm Cortex-M3 MCU, up to 128 KB Flash, 16 KB RAM, 4 KB EEPROM, USB, ADC, DAC, LCD (L152)
summary: A family of 32-bit Cortex-M3 microcontrollers built for low supply current, running to 32 MHz from 1.65 V to 3.6 V (1.8 V at power-on with BOR), with 32 KB to 128 KB of Flash, 10 KB or 16 KB of RAM and 4 KB of data EEPROM. It carries a 12-bit 1 Msps ADC, two DAC channels, two comparators, full-speed USB, three USARTs, two SPIs, two I2Cs, eight 16-bit timers, an RTC and capacitive touch channels; the STM32L152 adds an LCD driver. Standby draws 0.3 µA and Stop 0.57 µA typical. The STM32L151C8T6 is the LQFP48 part with 64 KB Flash, 10 KB RAM and 37 I/Os, for -40 °C to 85 °C, BOR on at power-up.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M3 with MPU, 32 kHz to 32 MHz, 33.3 DMIPS peak
Flash 32/64/128 KB with ECC, RAM 10/10/16 KB, data EEPROM 4 KB; C8T6: 64 KB / 10 KB / 4 KB
VDD 1.65 V to 3.6 V; 1.8 V min at power-on with BOR; VDDA 1.8 V min with ADC/DAC
214 µA/MHz in Run mode; 9.6 mA typ at 32 MHz range 1 (from Flash)
Low-power run 9 µA, Stop 0.57 µA (1.45 µA with RTC), Standby 0.3 µA (0.9 µA with RTC)
37/51/83 GPIOs by package, most 5 V tolerant; ±8 mA (±20 mA relaxed)
USB 2.0 FS, 3 × USART, 2 × SPI 16 Mbit/s, 2 × I2C, SWD/JTAG, ETM
LQFP48, UFQFPN48, LQFP64, TFBGA64, LQFP100, UFBGA100

notes: The order code adds the package letter (T: LQFP, U: UFQFPN, H: BGA), the temperature digit (6: -40 °C to 85 °C), an optional D (BOR off at power-up, VDD 1.65 V to 3.6 V; without it BOR is on and VDD is 1.8 V to 3.6 V) and an optional TR for tape and reel. STM32L151C8T6: no LCD, 48 pins, 64 KB Flash, LQFP48, -40 °C to 85 °C, BOR enabled.
Every part has 2 SPI, 2 I2C, 3 USART, 1 USB, 6 general-purpose and 2 basic timers, one 12-bit ADC, two 12-bit DAC channels, 2 comparators and 32 MHz maximum CPU clock.

circuits.title: Power supply scheme
circuits.description: How the supply pins are fed. The VDD rail goes to every VDD pin, with eleven 100 nF capacitors and one 4.7 µF capacitor across VDD and VSS. VDDA takes the same VDD rail and has 10 nF plus 1 µF to VSSA. VREF+ either joins VDDA or takes its own VREF rail, decoupled by 10 nF plus 1 µF; VREF- returns to VSSA.

notes: VREF+ may be joined to VDDA instead of a separate VREF rail.
VDD and VDDA are best fed from one source and may differ by up to 300 mV.

circuits.title: HSE oscillator circuit diagram
circuits.description: A crystal or ceramic resonator of 1 MHz to 24 MHz between OSC_IN and OSC_OUT, each end loaded to ground by a ceramic capacitor of 5 pF to 25 pF, normally equal. The feedback resistor RF (200 kΩ) and the amplifier with its consumption control are inside. The crystal's specified load is CL1 and CL2 in series plus about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance.
notes: The resonator and its capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as they can.
The value of the external resistor REXT depends on the crystal.

circuits.title: Typical application with a 32.768 kHz crystal
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT with a 5 pF to 15 pF ceramic capacitor from each end to ground. The feedback resistor RF (1.2 MΩ) and the bias-controlled gain stage are inside. A resonator with built-in capacitors can take the place of all three parts.
notes: The crystal's load capacitance is 7 pF or less, never 12.5 pF, so that CL1 and CL2 stay within 15 pF. With CL = 6 pF and Cstray = 2 pF, CL1 = CL2 = 8 pF.

circuits.title: Recommended NRST pin protection
circuits.description: NRST has an internal pull-up RPU to VDD, a Schmitt input and a filter ahead of the internal reset. Outside, 0.1 µF to ground protects against parasitic resets and a push button can pull the pin low.
notes: Whatever drives NRST takes it below VIL(NRST) max (0.8 V), or the reset is ignored.

operation.text: The STM32L151 and STM32L152 are pin- and software-compatible Cortex-M3 parts running at up to 32 MHz with an MPU, 32 KB to 128 KB of Flash with ECC, 10 KB or 16 KB of RAM and 4 KB of data EEPROM with ECC. The L152 adds an LCD driver with its own step-up converter; the L151 has none. Packages from 48 to 100 pins.

VDD (1.65 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/Os and the internal regulator. VDDA and VSSA feed the ADC, reset blocks, RC oscillators and PLL and connect to VDD and VSS; VDDA is 1.8 V minimum when the ADC is in use. Every power and ground pin is connected.

POR/PDR is built in, with a brownout reset that is either active at power-on (parts without suffix D: 1.8 V to 3.6 V) or off (suffix D: 1.65 V to 3.6 V). The option bytes set one of five BOR thresholds (1.8 V to 3 V) or switch BOR off for good, after which VDD may go to 1.65 V on any part. With BOR off at power-up, the supply ramp reaches 1.65 V on VDD at least 1 ms after VDD leaves the POR region. Start-up from power-on takes about 3.3 ms with BOR on, about 1 ms with it off. No external reset part is needed.
The PVD compares VDD/VDDA with one of seven software-chosen levels from 1.85 V to 3.05 V, in steps of about 200 mV, and can interrupt when the supply crosses it either way.

The core regulator has main mode (Run), low-power mode (Low-power run, Low-power sleep, Stop) and power-down (Standby, contents lost except the standby circuitry). Range 1 (VCORE 1.8 V) needs VDD of 2.0 V to 3.6 V and allows 32 MHz; range 2 (1.5 V) allows 16 MHz and range 3 (1.2 V) 4 MHz from the MSI, both over the full VDD range.

Sleep stops only the CPU. Low-power run runs from the MSI at its lowest setting (65 kHz) with the regulator in low-power mode; Low-power sleep is Sleep with the regulator in low-power mode. Stop keeps RAM and registers, stops the VCORE clocks and the PLL, MSI, HSI and HSE, and wakes in about 8 µs from any of 16 EXTI lines, the PVD, either comparator, the RTC events or USB wakeup; with RTC the LSE or LSI keeps running. Standby powers VCORE down and wakes in about 60 µs from NRST, the IWDG, a rising edge on one of three WKUP pins or, with RTC, an RTC alarm, tamper, timestamp or wakeup event. The RTC, the IWDG and their clocks keep running in Stop and Standby.
BOOT0 and BOOT1 (PB2) choose boot from Flash, from system memory or from RAM. The system memory holds a bootloader that programs the Flash over USART1 or USART2.

System clock sources: an HSE crystal of 1 MHz to 24 MHz, the 16 MHz HSI RC (±1 % factory-trimmed) and the MSI RC with seven settings from 65.5 kHz to 4.2 MHz, which can be trimmed against the LSE to ±0.5 %. The PLL takes HSE or HSI and has a 48 MHz output for USB. The RTC and LCD run from the LSE crystal (32.768 kHz), the 37 kHz LSI or the HSE; the LSI also clocks the IWDG. After reset the part runs from the MSI at 2.1 MHz. The clock security system moves to the HSI if the HSE fails. MCO puts an internal clock on a pin. AHB, APB1 and APB2 run at up to 32 MHz.
USB needs both the HSE and the PLL running, with the CPU at 24 MHz or 32 MHz; the 48 MHz clock comes from the PLL fed by the HSE crystal.

The RTC is a BCD calendar with alarms and a periodic wakeup from 120 µs to 36 hours, from Stop or Standby. It can be calibrated against an external 512 Hz output, with digital compensation for crystal error. Twenty 32-bit backup registers (80 bytes) stay powered in Standby and are cleared on tamper detection.

Each GPIO is push-pull or open-drain output, input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or alternate function, and can be locked. Most pins are 5 V tolerant (FT). The I/O block toggles at up to 16 MHz. The EXTI has 23 edge-detect lines: 16 shared by all GPIOs and 7 for the RTC, PVD, USB and comparators.
A GPIO sinks or sources ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH. The total sourced by all I/Os plus the Run current stays within IVDD (80 mA), and the total sunk within IVSS (80 mA).

The option bytes write-protect Flash in 4 KB sectors and set read protection: level 0 none; level 1 blocks Flash access while a debugger is connected or the part boots from RAM; level 2 disables debug and RAM boot permanently.
A 7-channel DMA moves data between memories, from peripherals to memory and from memory to peripherals, with circular buffers; it serves the SPI, I2C, USART, timers and ADC.

STM32L152 only: up to 8 commons and 44 segments (320 points), static, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/8 duty, static to 1/4 bias, blinking of up to 8 points, double-buffered RAM, operation in Stop mode. The internal step-up converter holds contrast independent of VDD and needs a capacitor Cext on VLCD; with it off, VLCD supplies the LCD voltage. Unused COM and SEG pins are GPIOs.

One 12-bit ADC with up to 24 external channels, single or scan mode, injected conversions, an analog watchdog, timer triggers, DMA, and a low-power mode with auto-shutdown that keeps full speed while the CPU runs slowly. It converts at up to 1 Msps from 2.4 V, 500 ksps from 1.8 V, and does not work below 1.8 V.

The sensor sits on ADC_IN16 and gives a voltage linear in temperature. Its offset varies part to part, so uncalibrated it suits only relative readings; each part carries factory readings at 30 °C and 110 °C (VDDA = 3 V) in system memory.

VREFINT, a bandgap of about 1.224 V on ADC_IN17, feeds the ADC and comparators; its factory reading at 30 °C and VDDA = 3 V is stored in system memory and allows VDD to be worked out without an external reference. It is also brought out on VREF_OUT (PB0 or PB1) through a low-power buffer good for about 1 µA, and can be switched off automatically in Stop.

Two 12-bit buffered DAC channels (resistor string and non-inverting amplifier), left or right aligned, with synchronized update, noise and triangle generation, DMA with underrun interrupt and eight trigger inputs from the timer update outputs. The reference is VREF+. The output buffer can be bypassed (BOFFx in DAC_CR).

Two comparators share bias and reference. COMP1 has a fixed threshold; COMP2 has inputs spanning both rails and a fast and a slow mode, and its threshold comes from the DAC, an I/O, VREFINT or 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 of VREFINT. Both wake the part from Stop and can be paired as a window comparator.
Up to 20 capacitive sensing channels in 10 analog I/O groups, acquired in software by charge transfer onto a sampling capacitor, with a few external parts.

TIM2, TIM3 and TIM4 are 16-bit up/down timers with four channels each (capture, compare, PWM, one-pulse), DMA, quadrature encoder and hall sensor inputs. TIM9 (two channels) and TIM10, TIM11 (one each) are 16-bit up-counters that can be clocked from the LSE. TIM6 and TIM7 are basic timers that trigger the DAC. A 24-bit SysTick, an independent watchdog (12-bit, LSI-clocked, runs in Stop and Standby) and a window watchdog (7-bit, main clock, early-warning interrupt) complete the set.

Two I2C (standard and fast mode, multimaster, SMBus 2.0/PMBus, hardware CRC, DMA). Three USARTs at up to 4 Mbit/s with CTS/RTS, IrDA, ISO 7816 and LIN. Two SPIs at up to 16 Mbit/s, master or slave, 8- or 16-bit frames, CRC for SD/MMC. One full-speed (12 Mbit/s) USB device, USB-IF certified, with suspend and resume; USB I/O levels need VDD of 3.0 V or more.
SDA and SCL are not genuine open-drain pins: in open-drain mode the PMOS to VDD is switched off but present.
A CRC unit computes a 32-bit CRC with a fixed polynomial, for example to check Flash integrity at run time. Each part has a 96-bit unique ID.

SWJ-DP gives JTAG or serial-wire debug; JTMS/JTCK are shared with SWDAT/SWCLK and a sequence on JTMS selects the port. JTAG can be disabled for good. The ETM streams trace through the TRACECLK and TRACED0 to TRACED3 pins.
The crystal or resonator and its load capacitors are placed as close to the oscillator pins as possible. The HSE feedback resistor is fairly low (200 kΩ), which resists humidity-induced leakage.

VDDA, and VREF+ when separate, are each decoupled by 1 µF in parallel with a smaller ceramic: 100 nF in the decoupling drawings, 10 nF in the guideline text, which asks for good-quality ceramics placed close to the chip. VREF+ and VREF- pins exist only on the 100-pin packages.
Negative current injected on an analog input degrades conversions on the other inputs; a Schottky diode from such a pin to ground is advised. Positive injection within the limits does not matter.
The UFQFPN48 has an exposed die pad underneath, soldered to PCB ground; all its pads are soldered for joint life.

Software deals with runaway conditions (corrupted program counter, unexpected reset, corrupted control registers). Most such faults can be provoked by holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s, or by ESD on the part.
